messages:
Ashley B: Heads-up — quiet spike in spot interruption rate for eu-west4-gpu yesterday evening. Not full outage but a lot of 1–2min blips across mixed pools.
Miguel R: saw that in the dashboard. raw interruption_rate jumped from 0.6% -> 3.8% over ~15m. alerts fired twice, then flapped.
Sam K: we need to stop paging on every blip. current alert is a 5m single-window threshold and it's too noisy for this metric.
Ashley B: agreed. Proposal: move to an ensemble signal that combines provider interruption API + our eviction_score + probe failures. Only alert when 2/3 signals exceed thresholds for 10m.
Jen L: +1. also add a smoothing layer: exponential moving avg (alpha 0.3) + min-duration 8m. That should prevent 1-minute noisy spikes from paging.
Miguel R: can you sketch config? e.g.

```
signal_ensemble:
  components: [provider_interrupt, eviction_score, probe_fail_rate]
  combine: majority
  window: 10m
  smoothing: ema(alpha=0.3)
  min_alert_duration: 8m
```

Sam K: looks good. also suggest a quick cost/regret calc so paging threshold ties to SLO impact.
Ashley B: I ran a quick backtest: when interruption_rate sustained at 3% for 10m in eu-west4, we saw ~1.8% increase in 99th-token-latency due to retries and cold-starts for a subset of routes. translates to ~0.4% user error-rate on tail-sensitive features.
ops-oncall: what's the customer-visible threshold we want? i.e., when does infra actually affect SLO enough to page?
Jen L: let's map interruption->capacity_loss->SLO_impact. simple conversion we used earlier: capacity_loss = interruption_rate * avg_instance_utilization. SLO_impact ~= capacity_loss * sensitivity_factor(route). We should default sensitivity_factor=1 for inference routes and 0.3 for async embedding jobs.
Miguel R: want to cap spurious page noise: only page when estimated SLO_impact > 0.5% AND ensemble_alert true.
Sam K: add a recovery suppression: once paged, suppress further pages for same region+pool for 30m unless impact grows >2x.
Ashley B: ops: we also need a dashboard widget: "ensemble interrupt health" showing each component, the combined score, estimated SLO impact, and cost delta if we failover to on-demand.
ops-oncall: for runbooks, document exact failover policy: 1) attempt soft-fallback to mixed on-demand nodes for affected routes, 2) if latency/SLO still breached after 5m, scale dedicated pool or route to redundant region.
Jen L: does anyone have objections to the EM A smoothing alpha=0.3? I tested alpha=0.2/0.3/0.5 on last 30 days — 0.3 balanced responsiveness and noise suppression best.
Miguel R: fine by me. we should codify the backtest results as a unit test in the alerting repo so we don't regress.
Ashley B: I'll open the PR with config + dashboard json + backtest snippet. will include sample query and the little cost calc.
infra-bot: alerting-config: PR opened by Ashley B (#4123) — diff adds ensemble signal + smoothing + suppression rules.
Sam K: once PR lands let's run it in canary for a week for eu-west4 only.
ops-oncall: noted. I'll set a temporary team's escalation policy for the canary window.
Jen L: one more ask: add a small synthetic probe that requests short completions at 75% of typical seq len to measure degradation in a representative way.
Ashley B: will add probe and add probe_fail_rate as component. thanks everyone.
Miguel R: thanks — this should reduce noisy pages while preserving response to real capacity issues. :thumbsup:
